coin.definition: A small round piece of metal used as money.

bill.definition: An itemized statement of money owed for goods shipped or services rendered.

penny.definition: A fractional monetary unit of Ireland and the United Kingdom.

nickel.definition: A United States coin worth one twentieth of a dollar.

dime.definition: A United States coin worth one tenth of a dollar.

quarter.definition: A United States coin worth twenty-five cents.

dollar.definition: A United States coin worth one dollar.

euro.definition: The basic monetary unit of most members of the European Union (introduced in 1999).

pound.definition: United States writer who lived in Europe.

yen.definition: A yearning for something or to do something.

bank-account.definition: Money kept with a bank can be accessed through this account by a person or organization. It supports withdrawals and payments, including transfers, checks, and debit-card purchases.

savings.definition: Money kept aside for future use rather than spent now.

checking.definition: A bank account lets you write checks, pay bills, and withdraw money for everyday needs. It is meant for spending, not saving.

deposit.definition: Money put into a bank account.

withdrawal.definition: Money taken out of a bank account.

atm.definition: A means of digital communications that is capable of very high speeds.

balance.definition: Equality between the totals of the credit and debit sides of an account.

statement.definition: A message that is stated or declared.

interest.definition: A fixed charge for borrowing money.

transfer.definition: A person who transfers or is transferred from one position to another.

cash.definition: Money in the form of notes and coins.

credit-card.definition: A plastic or metal payment card from a bank or other lender lets its holder buy goods and services with borrowed money up to a set limit, then repay the balance, usually with interest, an extra charge for borrowing.

debit-card.definition: A payment card that lets you buy goods or withdraw cash using funds taken directly from your bank account.

check.definition: A written order directing a bank to pay money.

receipt.definition: A written or digital record showing that a payment was made.

invoice.definition: An itemized statement of money owed for goods shipped or services rendered.

wallet.definition: A pocket-size case for holding papers and paper money.

price.definition: The property of having material worth (often indicated by the amount of money something would bring if sold).

cost.definition: The property of having material worth (often indicated by the amount of money something would bring if sold).

discount.definition: Interest on an annual basis deducted in advance on a loan.

tax.definition: Money collected by a government to pay for public services.

budget.definition: A sum of money allocated for a particular purpose.

expense.definition: Amounts paid for goods and services that may be currently tax deductible (as opposed to capital expenditures).

affordable.definition: That you have the financial means for.

expensive.definition: High in price or charging high prices.

cheap.definition: Relatively low in price or charging low prices.

income.definition: The financial gain (earned or unearned) accruing over a given period of time.

salary.definition: A fixed amount of money paid regularly for a job.

wage.definition: Money paid for work, often calculated by the hour.

debt.definition: The state of owing something (especially money).

loan.definition: The temporary provision of money (usually at interest).

mortgage.definition: A conditional conveyance of property as security for the repayment of a loan.

insurance.definition: Promise of reimbursement in the case of loss.

investment.definition: Money put into an asset or business in the hope of a return.

profit.definition: Money left after a business pays its costs.

loss.definition: The amount by which the cost of a business exceeds its revenue.
